parsed.why: Reading-down decriminalises private acts, but no gender-identity protection, police documented dismissing anti-LGBT attacks, a killing of someone read as gender-nonconforming, and evangelical hostility aimed at tourists. Thin trans data; hostile-policing, thin-recourse tier.

No trans criminal exposure; hate-crime law covers gender identity, marker change since 2013, trans-specific search rules, centres and tourism tolerance. Deductions: enforcement gaps, inadequate hate-crime investigations, under-reporting, hinterland hostility, unresolved border-document treatment.

Sodomy statute with 14-year terms, sporadic enforcement, and police documented as a main perpetrator of rape and beatings against trans people with impunity — state-tolerated targeting plus criminal law. One sanctuary village and third-gender traditions do not offset that.

State-imposed universal exposure: sex-at-birth passport and visa policy, border refusal for marker mismatch, lifetime-ineligibility risk, facility bans with trespass arrests, custody harm. Foreign governments issue advisories; no working remedy for the outed traveller.

Decriminalised 2025, and the gender-neutral domestic-violence act expressly protects gender identity with equal remedies, plus police/port/prison sensitisation training. Offset by conservative society, opposition to the UN SOGI declaration, and dated visitor-directed violence.
